locator: §3.4, 'Since this sort of explanation makes reference to our purposes in using moral terms rather than to an independent realm of moral fact, Blackburn thinks it supports a quasi-realist account rather than a straightforward realist theory.'
interpretation: Blackburn (1993, 137): moral judgments must supervene on judgments about natural properties because their point is 'to guide desires and choices among the natural features of the world'. Read as a quasi-realist grounding answer: what explains the shape of moral truth is the purpose of moral talk, not an independent realm of moral fact. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
